title: Moove Raises Series C for AV Infrastructure
summary: Moove announced on August 5, 2026 that it raised $250 million in Series C funding, valuing the company at $2.1 billion. The round was led by Mubadala Investment Company, Woven Capital, Toyota's Growth Fund and Ion Pacific, with participation from BlackRock, Uber, MUFG, Franklin Templeton and others. Moove will use the funding to expand its autonomous-vehicle business, including fleet ownership and robotics-first depot infrastructure it calls 'Nests,' where autonomous fleets are charged, serviced, maintained and orchestrated for continuous operation. The company, already a third-party fleet operator for Waymo in Phoenix and Miami with planned London operations, expects to grow its AV-focused workforce more than 220% by year-end, from about 150 to 500 employees.
whyItMatters: As robotaxi and autonomous-fleet deployments scale, the physical infrastructure to charge, service and orchestrate those fleets around the clock is becoming its own capital-intensive category, distinct from the driving software itself. Moove's raise is a bet that owning and operating this 'infrastructure layer' for autonomy, much like data centers underpin cloud AI, will be as strategically important as the autonomy stack, and that operators like Waymo will increasingly outsource fleet logistics rather than build it themselves.
